cells.tense: You are here inside the clearing, holding what you have without forcing a door.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're keeping alive through the ending, and let one person see you do it this week.
cells.core:
You're in the middle of an ending that has to finish before something else can start, and you're holding on. Not gripping — holding. Persisting through it the way you do, and it doesn't look like bracing anymore. It looks like someone who has done this before.

The strength in you comes from not giving up on what was worth hoping for, and that's rare in a clearing. Most people either grip or drop it. You're standing here with the hope still lit, waiting for what comes next to show itself. Nothing is being forced open. And you're free to feed that patience a little more — tell someone what you're keeping lit, and let that be enough for today.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the hope, not forcing the clearing.
cells.verb: keeping going, expecting the light to come back around

cells.tense: You are already living past this ending before it has been allowed to finish.
cells.ask: Let one thing this week end unanswered, and hold what you know without bringing it up.
cells.core:
You're bracing at something that hasn't opened yet — the next chapter, the resolution, the proof that this all worked. That far ahead, everything is still intact, so none of the clearing here gets to finish. You keep pushing past the ending, and the hope you're carrying turns into the thing you're using to skip it.

What you know is real and it's steady. It doesn't need to be said to be true. This week, let one thing go unresolved on purpose — a conversation, a question, a last word you've been holding ready. Leave it. See what happens when you don't rush to the part where it's already okay again.
cells.sheetLine: You're skipping the clearing to get to the part where it's fine.

cells.tense: You are at a door that has already shut behind you, still facing it.
cells.ask: Do one small thing this week that outlives today — plant it, feed it, keep its shape.
cells.core:
The hope that carried you through everything before keeps moving, and it turns into something you tend instead of something you wait inside. The ending finishes, and what outlasts it gets your hands. That's steady here.

The ending has happened, and the door is where you're facing. The hope that carried you has gone quiet, and the clearing has become the place you stay, not the place you move through. You don't need more strength pushed at that door. You need something growing, that asks for your hands and not your hope. Pick one thing that outlives this week and tend it — not to replace what ended, but because your hands remember how.

cells.tense: You are already holding the clearing steady while calling it something else entirely.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that one thing you've kept going through this and call it yours.
cells.core:
Someone in your life would say you've been the one holding things together through this ending. You'd probably say you're just doing what needed to be done. But the persistence is running — that's the same stubborn hope that carried you through everything before, and it's working here too.

You've been calling it circumstance, or timing, or just getting through. It isn't. It's you, doing this, however the door stays open and the room stays clear. Say it once, plainly, about one thing you've kept going through this — that it's yours. Nobody else has to hear it. Just don't keep calling it nothing.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding this together. You haven't said so yet.
